local.title: Slopes, older shrubs and **wetland edges.**
local.intro: Brandon Township's plan names rolling hills, woods, wetlands and lakes as the reason people move here. Landscaping around Ortonville has to fit that ground: beds on banks, shrubs that have had decades to grow, and soil near water that needs covering fast.

points.title: Walls for sloped beds
points.body: Rolling ground means beds on banks. A boulder wall or a low block wall gives a sloped bed a level shelf, the way a curved boulder wall can hold a newly graded slope below a deck.

points.title: Shrubs from the 1980s
points.body: A typical Brandon Township home dates to the mid 1980s, so many foundation shrubs have had about forty years to outgrow their spots. Digging them out by the roots, as with one reviewer's 25 year old bushes, lets the bed start clean.

points.title: Near the creek and wetlands
points.body: The township plan names sediment as the main problem in Kearsley Creek, and bare ground is one of the causes. A bed rebuilt near a ditch, creek or wetland edge gets mulched right away so the soil stays in place.

points.title: Invasive plants to watch
points.body: Brandon Township says phragmites are common here and Asian bittersweet turns up too. If either has crept into a bed or a tree line, point it out at the walk through; the township has guidance on dealing with both.

logistics.title: How an Ortonville landscaping job runs.
body: Rob comes out, walks the yard and the slopes, suggests what to keep and what to replace, then quotes it. On bigger properties a compact track loader does the digging, so old shrubs come out roots and all and the trailer hauls them off.

Once the beds are shaped and edged, fabric goes down where it helps, then 2 to 3 inches of mulch kept back from trunks and stems. For upkeep afterward, ask about [landscape maintenance](/landscape-maintenance/); for bare or rough ground, see [grading and new lawns](/grading-and-new-lawns/).

faq.q: Do you do landscaping in Ortonville, MI?
faq.a: Yes. Grand Scapes does landscaping in Ortonville and Brandon Township: bed makeovers, shrub and small tree removal, block walls, boulders and natural edges, plants, fabric and mulch. The estimate is free.

faq.q: Can you build a bed on a slope?
faq.a: Yes. On a rolling Ortonville lot, a boulder wall or block wall gives the bed a level shelf so soil and mulch stay where they were put. Rob will suggest which edge suits the grade and the look of the house.

Yes, roots and all, and small trees too. One reviewer had 25 year old bushes and a cherry tree taken out, the bed rebuilt with black mesh and mulch, and a natural edge cut, all in two days. Big trees go to a tree crew. See [bush removal](/bush-removal/).

faq.q: When is a good time for landscaping in Ortonville?
faq.a: Any time the ground can be worked, spring through fall. If an oak stands near the work, Brandon Township says not to prune oaks in the warmer months, and MSU Extension puts the riskiest stretch at April 15 to July 15, so any oak cuts wait for cold weather.
